unit.why: A single anecdote about R. Meir of Premishlan at a meal, insisting a four-penny coin is worth five, with the compiler's kabbalistic interpretation appended.
unit.boundary_note: trailing 'מענין מנגן' is the heading of the next division

stories.start_quote: סיפרו לי מעשה רב מהה״ק מוהרמ״מ
stories.summary_en: At a festive meal R. Meir of Premishlan sends a servant to buy beer with a four-penny coin, insists against the vendor that it is worth five, quarrels with the servant until the disciples signal him to concede, and then prays 'that all the world should know that a four is a five', which the compiler explains as a mystical unification according to the Zohar.
